blocks.text: Summary of the Original Preface

inline.s: Through the ages countless people have for the most part been bound by destiny, unable to make their own decisions. Only those of great goodness cannot be bound by destiny; this is what is meant by saying that the perfected person holds the key to creating destiny.

Only those of great goodness cannot be bound by fate; this is what is meant by saying that the perfected person holds the key to transforming destiny! [◆ qishu: fortune, fate. zhiren: a person of exceedingly lofty moral cultivation.])

Liaofan's Four Lessons is known throughout the world as a treasure book for transforming destiny. A person of great blessings, once he obtains this book, naturally recites it with whole-hearted reverence, never tiring of reading it a hundred times, and passes from understanding to practice. And so he turns illness into health, poverty into prosperity, transgression into blessing, and the ordinary into the sagely. By it one cultivates oneself, and everyone may become a sage or worthy; by it one cultivates the world, and the whole world may dissolve its disasters and hindrances. This is the gateway of skillful means for saving oneself and saving others!

Here, “you have sat for three days and I have seen not one deluded thought arise” means that Master Liaofan sat in quiet meditation for three days and was able to concentrate his mind on one point, free of distracting thoughts. Note: in the practice of Chan concentration there are four stages: the first, second, third and fourth dhyana. Before the first dhyana come the coarse abiding, the subtle abiding, the concentration of the realm of desire, and the concentration not yet reached. In the first dhyana, the breath stops. When the outer breath stops, the inner breath becomes active, as in hibernation. At such a time the mind is clear as water and bright as a mirror. This may last a day, or even a month or a year, without the settled mind decaying. Master Liaofan later wrote a piece entitled Essential Methods of Quiet Sitting. In its preface he says: “My teacher, the Great Master Yungu, sat in quiet meditation for more than twenty years and wondrously attained the legacy of Tiantai, and he spoke to me of it in full detail.” [Tiantai] that is, the Tiantai school. “Tiantai” is the name of a mountain in Tiantai county, Taizhou, in Zhejiang province; in the Sui dynasty the Great Zhiyi lived on this mountain and founded a school, and later ages therefore called his school the Tiantai school, abbreviated to Tiantai or the Tai school. The Great Zhiyi wrote a one-fascicle work, Calm and Insight for Beginners, known to the world as the Lesser Calm and Insight of Tiantai, which is the essential method for cultivating calm and insight in sitting
